<!--

## Breaking change

The DLNA-DMR integration migrated to configuration via the UI. Configuring DLNA-DMR via YAML configuration has been deprecated and will be removed in a future Home Assistant release.

Your existing YAML configuration is automatically imported on upgrade to this release; and thus can be safely removed from your YAML configuration after upgrading.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This PR adds config-flow configuration for the `dlna_dmr` component, and deprecates YAML configuration. It is a big change, and in support of this, it also adds unit tests and strict mypy checking.

## Type of change
<!--
  What type of change does your PR introduce to Home Assistant?
  NOTE: Please, check only 1! box!
  If your PR requires multiple boxes to be checked, you'll most likely need to
  split it into multiple PRs. This makes things easier and faster to code review.
-->

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New integration (thank you!)
- [x] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information
<!--
  Details are important, and help maintainers processing your PR.
  Please be sure to fill out additional details, if applicable.
-->

The primary aim of this pull request is to add config-flow support and SSDP auto-discovery to the `dlna_dmr` component. It already supported SSDP, but disabled-by-default, using the legacy `discovery` component; now it's done using `DlnaDmrFlowHandler.async_step_ssdp`.

I've also improved the handling of unavailable devices, re-using the `ssdp` component for device availability notifications instead of polling for missing devices on the network. This might lead to a slightly increased delay for when devices become available within HA when turned on (from 10 seconds `async_update` polling interval to 1 minute SSDP search). If a device is not available when HA starts up then the entity will still be created, in an unavailable state.

To aid development, I've added strict typing and unit tests.

I've also added @StevenLooman to the code owners, as he is the original author of the component, but the code owners was blank.

- Link to documentation pull request: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/19087

@bdraco Thank you for the code review. I'll figure out what is going on with the import attempts and come back with further comments/changes.

@bdraco I've looked into the failed import attempts and I think they've failed because the device is off when HA starts (I've added extra logging to confirm). They should be picked up via SSDP when they're next turned on, but any extra settings (`listen_port`, `name`,  and `callback_url_override`) from the YAML config won't be imported. Is this limitation acceptable, or should it make more effort to contact the device (e.g. polling for it)?

I've updated the config-flow to apply settings from configuration.yml to added devices if they weren't already migrated. This should catch the case of a device being off when HA starts and turned on after.

@StevenLooman Thank you for the code review.

The [SSDP PR](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/55540) looks like something I've wanted too, and I am happy to submit a follow-up PR to the `dlna_dmr` component to use it when both of these PRs get merged. I think calling `DlnaDmrEntity._device_disconnect` should suffice for a BYEBYE, and `DlnaDmrEntity._device_connect` for an ALIVE. The UPDATE case is more complicated, but can probably be handled by disconnect followed by connect (when the location changes), like in `DlnaDmrEntity.async_config_update_listener`.

> When the media renderer device is an embedded device, the actual `deviceType` in `info_with_desc` (in `homeassistant.components.ssdp.Scanner._ssdp_listener_callback`) is for the root device, not the embedded device, thus the domain is not matched. > Added 3 devices (2x Symfonisk, 1x TV.) Removing 1x Symfonisk is ok, from then on removing a device results in this error:

Ugh, I just spotted [my error](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/55267/files#diff-1a430fcc1ceb0948e838d4aca53a83eb08589a2a10b0305bdb61456d68a70217R142). Auto-initialised class-level attributes are a bad idea for lists.

Discovery is now done based on Service Type (ST, as sent for M-SEARCH responses) and Notification Type (NT, as sent for ssdp:alive advertisements). The unique_id is now derived from the embedded device's UDN, not the root device, so this might show a double discovery if you've been testing your own local branch.

This PR now has a dependency on https://github.com/StevenLooman/async_upnp_client/pull/86 and won't pass CI until that is merged. I'll update this PR when it is.

issue_context.title: Platform dlna_dmr does not generate unique IDs
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I noticed the following error showing up in the error log. I've never seen it before:

```
Logger: homeassistant.components.media_player
Source: helpers/entity_platform.py:492
Integration: Media player (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 6:59:09 PM (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 6:59:09 PM

Platform dlna_dmr does not generate unique IDs. ID uuid:30516621-cfad-e766-716a-2cb9d1dd98cd already exists - ignoring media_player.oled65gx9la
```

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.3.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

Media player

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/media_player

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
# Put your YAML below this line
# discover DLNA
discovery:
  enable:
    - dlna_dmr
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
# Put your logs below this line
2021-03-21 03:18:32 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.media_player] Updating dlna_dmr media_player took longer than the scheduled update interval 0:00:10

2021-03-21 18:59:09 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.media_player] Platform dlna_dmr does not generate unique IDs. ID uuid:30516621-cfad-e766-716a-2cb9d1dd98cd already exists - ignoring media_player.oled65gx9la
```
comments:
Hi,

I got this error when I set both discovery and media_player.

No error when I set only media_player directive.

With only discovery, my dlna device is not discovered at all.

dlna xml description can be retreived using gssdp-discover command (gupnp-tools package).

Best regards.
The `dlna_dmr` component should be updated to support normal config flows. I believe somebody is working on this, but not sure how fast s/he is going.

There hasn't been any activity on this issue recently. Due to the high number of incoming GitHub notifications, we have to clean some of the old issues, as many of them have already been resolved with the latest updates.
Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue has now been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.

review_comments: Should the whole domain be marked as deprecated?
Has my preference. By the looks of it all options can be set via the OptionsFlow.

The `dlna_dmr` yaml config is done as a platform within the `media_player` domain, and gets used like so:
```
media_player:
  - platform: dlna_dmr
    url: http://fake/fake.xml
```

I'm not sure how to mark this as deprecated, since `cv.deprecated` only applies to keys, not key/value combos.
I think we have done a logger message with level of warning that it's deprecated advising removal of the yaml config in the past for this case.
Thanks for the example, and done.
This is not a good pattern. We want the config flow to be isolated from the rest of the integration. The flow should just return the config flow result.
All entity state update callbacks must be registered in `async_added_to_hass` and unregistered on entity remove.
Don't use `STATE_UNKNOWN` directly. We use `None` to represent unknown state. It will be converted in the entity base class.
This one was already addressed in #56728

This way of importing platform config is not robust. It doesn't catch all accepted ways of writing the YAML for platforms. We should import the platform config from `async_setup_platform` in the media_player platform instead.

This looks similar to https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/56431

We should clean this up in a new PR once both merge.
Working on that PR when time is available, though this PR has more priority at the moment.
Mostly to satisfy linting. HA's pylint configuration disables the `unused-argument` warning, but I've gotten into the habit of using `del` to indicate that it's intentional.

Do we really want to let users enter a URL? I doubt many would understand what to do here.

Perhaps it would be better to do a 'manual' SSDP scan here (although, this is already covered by the ssdp step), or leave this option out.

The latter option reduces the supported cases, but makes things less confusing, I think.

Indeed, most users should be supported by the automatic SSDP discovery step. This, like the `listen_port` and `callback_url_override` are meant for the case that SSDP is broken for some reason (e.g. as you said multi-network installations, or when HA is behind a NAT or firewall).

I originally had code to let users pick from a list of discovered devices, then realised that the discovery was done in the exact same way as the usual ssdp step, so it didn't actually provide any benefits. Superfluous code still needs to be tested, so I removed the code instead.
We're not allowed to use the sync api inside the event loop. Please use `self.async_write_ha_state` instead.
